clauses.evidence: keywords[0] = DEFENDER ([cast]: 'keywords +DEFENDER'). The standard board always holds your 4/4 (you_giant), so the permission below applies in every attack stimulus and the trace never shows defender stopping an attack. Packs on the live tree: I10_1 (creatures with power 3 or less: it is never asked to attack), I10_3 (only the opponent has 4+ power creatures: never asked), I10_5 (the 4-power creature left: never asked), I10_6 (it still blocks: it kills a 2/2 attacker).

clauses.clause: As long as you control a creature with power 4 or greater, this creature can attack as though it didn't have defender.
clauses.evidence: The true case is in the trace: [stimulus: this creature attacks alone, unblocked] and [... opp_giant blocks it]: 'card becomes tapped', DECLARE_ATTACKERS, 3 combat damage to the opponent (with your 4/4 you_giant on the board). The false case, the other player's creatures, and the bounds are never shown. Tree abilities[0] (the compiler's B5a-aslong-attack-despite-defender form): static ATTACK_POLICY scope AS_NO_DEFENDER on this creature, condition QTY_GE 1 over creatures you control with QTY_GE 4 POWER (itself included, no 'another'). Packs on the live tree: I10_2 (a creature of power exactly 4 enables it: attacks for 3), I10_1 (power 3 does not), I10_3 (the opponent's 5/5 and 6/6 do not), I10_4 (a Tyrannodon with a +1/+1 counter is a 4/4 and attacks alone for 4), I10_5 (the 4-power creature leaves before combat: no attack). I10_7 (a noncreature artifact with printed power 5 does not count: it is a creature you need). Control, not ownership: I10_8 (a stolen 5/5 enables the attack), I10_9 (your only 4-power creature taken: no attack).
